za-dynasty.s: The Za dynasty was an early ruling dynasty of the Songhai people, centred on Gao in the bend of the Niger River. A Songhai kingdom under the Za dynasty existed for generations as a tributary state within the Mali Empire.

zabt-system.s: The zabt system was a method of land revenue assessment in the Mughal Empire, developed under Akbar and associated with his minister Todar Mal. Land was measured and classified, and the tax was fixed in cash on the basis of average yields and prices over several years.

zacatecas.s: Zacatecas is a city in north-central Mexico founded after the discovery of rich silver deposits in 1546. It became one of the most productive silver-mining centres of New Spain.

zafarnama.s: The Zafarnama, or Book of Victory, is a Persian chronicle of the life and conquests of Timur, written under Timurid patronage. Versions were composed by Nizam al-Din Shami and later by Sharaf al-Din Ali Yazdi.

zaghawa.s: The Zaghawa are a people of the eastern Sahara and Sahel, living in present-day Chad and Sudan. Early Arabic writers used the name for the rulers and people of the region around Lake Chad.

zagros-mountains.s: The Zagros Mountains are a long mountain range in western Iran, stretching from the borders of Turkey to the Persian Gulf and separating the Mesopotamian plain from the Iranian plateau. Their highland peoples repeatedly pressed on Mesopotamian states, including the Akkadian…

zagwe-dynasty.s: The Zagwe dynasty was a ruling dynasty of the northern Ethiopian highlands that rose to power after the decline of Aksum, from around 940 CE according to the chronology. It is best known for the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, built under its king of that name.

zaju.s: Zaju is a form of Chinese drama combining spoken dialogue, song and music, which reached its classical form under the Yuan Dynasty. Its four-act plays treated historical, romantic and moral themes.

zakat.s: Zakat is the obligatory almsgiving of Islam, one of the Five Pillars, levied as a proportion of certain kinds of wealth and distributed to the poor and other specified recipients. In Islamic states it also functioned as a tax.

zaman-shah-durrani.s: Zaman Shah Durrani was ruler of the Durrani Empire of Afghanistan in the 1790s, a grandson of Ahmad Shah Durrani. He launched several invasions of the Punjab.

zambezi.s: The Zambezi is the fourth-longest river in Africa, flowing from Zambia through Angola, along the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe, and across Mozambique to the Indian Ocean. It was a major route for trade between the interior and the coast.

zambia.s: Zambia is a landlocked country in south-central Africa, including part of the Central African Copperbelt. Accounts of the Lunda Empire place the empire's origins in a region spanning the south-east of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Angola and parts…

zanata-berbers.s: The Zanata were one of the major Berber confederations of North Africa, many of them pastoral nomads of the Maghreb and the northern Sahara. They played a large role in the politics of the medieval Maghreb, later founding the Marinid and Zayyanid dynasties.

zand-dynasty.s: The Zand dynasty ruled much of Iran from about 1751 to 1794, founded by Karim Khan Zand, a chief of the Zand tribe of the Zagros. Karim Khan governed from Shiraz under the title of Vakil, bringing a period of relative peace after the collapse of the Afsharid Empire.

zanj-rebellion.s: The Zanj Rebellion was a major revolt in southern Iraq from 869 to 883, led by Ali ibn Muhammad and involving enslaved East Africans, known as the Zanj, who laboured in the salt marshes near Basra. The rebels established a state, sacked Basra and defeated Abbasid armies for…

zara-yaqob.s: Zara Yaqob was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1434 to 1468, one of the most powerful rulers of the Solomonic dynasty. He centralised royal authority, reformed the Ethiopian Church and promoted religious literature.

zaragoza.s: Zaragoza is a city in north-eastern Spain on the Ebro River, in the medieval period the capital of an important taifa kingdom of al-Andalus. It was the most important Almoravid city in north-eastern Spain.

zaria.s: Zaria is a city in northern Nigeria, historically the capital of the Hausa state of Zazzau. It became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate after the jihad of the early nineteenth century.

zarpanitu.s: Zarpanitu was a Babylonian goddess, the consort of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon. Her statue stood with his in the Esagila temple.

zayyanid-dynasty.s: The Zayyanid dynasty was a Berber dynasty that ruled the central Maghreb from Tlemcen, in present-day Algeria, from the thirteenth to the sixteenth century. Of Zanata origin, it emerged from the fragmentation of the Almohad Caliphate.

zeila.s: Zeila is a port town on the Gulf of Aden coast in present-day Somaliland, historically a major outlet for trade between the Ethiopian highlands and the Red Sea and Indian Ocean. Accounts of the Adal Sultanate record that Sabr ad-Din III reconstituted the Walashma state at…

zemene-mesafint.s: The Zemene Mesafint, or Era of the Princes, was a period of Ethiopian history from 1769 until the mid-nineteenth century, in which the emperors were largely powerless and regional lords held real authority. Many emperors occupied the throne while real governance passed to Ras…

zeng-guofan.s: Zeng Guofan was a Chinese scholar-official and military leader who raised and commanded the Xiang Army, which played a central role in suppressing the Taiping Rebellion. He was also a leading figure in the Self-Strengthening Movement.

zengid-dynasty.s: The Zengid dynasty was a Turkic dynasty that ruled northern Iraq and Syria in the twelfth century, founded by Imad al-Din Zengi, who captured Edessa from the Crusaders in 1144. His son Nur al-Din extended Zengid power and sent forces into Fatimid Egypt.

zerafshan.s: The Zerafshan is a river of Central Asia that flows west from the mountains of Tajikistan through Uzbekistan, watering the oases of Samarkand and Bukhara. Its valley was one of the richest agricultural and commercial regions of Transoxiana.

zheng-family.s: The Zheng family was a maritime trading and military clan of south-eastern China, led by Zheng Zhilong and his son Zheng Chenggong, known in the West as Koxinga. Remaining loyal to the Ming, they resisted the Qing conquest and in 1662 seized Taiwan from the Dutch.

zheng-he.s: Zheng He was a Chinese admiral and court eunuch who led seven great maritime expeditions for the Ming Empire between 1405 and 1433. His fleets of large treasure ships sailed through Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean as far as Arabia and East Africa, establishing tributary…

zhizhi.s: Zhizhi was a Xiongnu chanyu of the first century BCE, a brother and rival of Huhanye during the civil war that split the Xiongnu Empire. While Huhanye submitted to the Han Dynasty, Zhizhi led his followers westward.

zhu-wen.s: Zhu Wen was a Chinese military leader who first fought as a rebel under Huang Chao and then served the Tang Dynasty before turning against it. In 907 he forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate and founded the Later Liang dynasty.

zhu-xi.s: Zhu Xi was a Chinese philosopher of the Southern Song Dynasty and the leading figure of Neo-Confucianism. His synthesis of Confucian ethics and metaphysics, and his commentaries on the Four Books, later became the basis of the imperial civil service examinations.

ziggurat.s: A ziggurat is a massive stepped temple tower built in ancient Mesopotamia and Elam, with a shrine on its summit. Ziggurats were constructed of mud brick, often faced with baked brick, and served as the centre of a city's religious life.

ziggurat-of-ur.s: The Ziggurat of Ur is a great stepped temple tower at the ancient city of Ur in southern Iraq, dedicated to the moon god Nanna. It was built by Ur-Nammu and completed by his son Shulgi in the twenty-first century BCE.

zimbabwe.s: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa, whose name derives from the stone enclosures of Great Zimbabwe. Its plateau was home to a succession of states built on gold, cattle and trade, including the Mutapa Empire and the Rozvi Empire.

zimbabwean-plateau.s: The Zimbabwean plateau is a high plateau in southern Africa between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers, rich in gold and suited to cattle herding. It was the setting of Great Zimbabwe and later of the Mutapa and Rozvi states.

zimri-lim.s: Zimri-Lim was the last king of Mari, a city-state on the middle Euphrates in present-day Syria, in the eighteenth century BCE. His palace archive is a major source for the period.

zinkekra.s: Zinkekra is an archaeological site in the Fezzan region of south-western Libya, a fortified hilltop settlement above the Wadi al-Ajal. Accounts of the Garamantian Empire identify the citadel at Zinkekra as the royal centre of the Garamantes during their formative phase.

zionism.s: Zionism is the nationalist movement that emerged in the late nineteenth century to establish a Jewish national homeland in Palestine. Its political form was founded by Theodor Herzl, whose writings and organisation of the first Zionist Congress in 1897 gave it international…

zirid-dynasty.s: The Zirid dynasty was a Sanhaja Berber dynasty that governed Ifriqiya, roughly present-day Tunisia and eastern Algeria, on behalf of the Fatimid Caliphate after the Fatimids moved to Egypt. Between about 1048 and 1052 the Zirid governor abandoned Ismaili Shi'ism for Sunni…

zliten-mosaic.s: The Zliten Mosaic is a Roman floor mosaic found at a villa at Zliten, near Leptis Magna in Libya, depicting gladiatorial combat and the killing of prisoners by wild animals in the arena. It shows lions and leopards supplied by the Garamantes being used in Roman arenas.

zoroastrianism.s: Zoroastrianism is an ancient Iranian religion founded on the teachings of the prophet Zoroaster, centred on the worship of Ahura Mazda and the struggle between good and evil. It was the state religion of the Sasanian Empire, whose kings drew legitimacy from it.

zoskales.s: Zoskales was a king associated with Aksum in the first century CE, the earliest Aksumite ruler named in a written source. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes him as Greek-educated.

zubayrids.s: The Zubayrids were the supporters of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who claimed the caliphate from Mecca during the Second Fitna after the death of Yazid I in 683. For several years they controlled much of the Islamic world.

zulu-kingdom.s: The Zulu Kingdom was a powerful state in south-eastern Africa built by Shaka from the 1810s onward through military reform and conquest. Its rise was associated with the Mfecane, a period of warfare and migration that spread across southern Africa.

zumbo.s: Zumbo was a trading settlement on the Zambezi River, in present-day Mozambique near the borders of Zambia and Zimbabwe. Gold exports were channelled through coastal trading fairs at Zumbo and Masekesa.

zwangendaba.s: Zwangendaba was a Nguni military leader who led the Ngoni people northwards from south-eastern Africa during the upheavals of the Mfecane in the early nineteenth century. Accounts of the Rozvi Empire record that Zwangendaba's Ngoni crossed the Zimbabwean plateau from…

zhang-er.s: Zhang Er was a statesman from the former state of Wei who joined the revolt against the Qin and helped restore the kingdom of Zhao. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Changshan, but his former friend Chen Yu drove him out with help from Qi, and he joined Liu Bang.

zhang-han.s: Zhang Han was the last great general of the Qin dynasty. He crushed Chen Sheng's rebellion and defeated Xiang Liang, but after the Qin defeat at Julu he surrendered to Xiang Yu in 207 BCE.

zang-tu.s: Zang Tu was a general of the revived state of Yan who followed Xiang Yu against the Qin. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Yan, and he killed his former lord Han Guang to take Liaodong as well.

zhao-shanzheng.s: Zhao Shanzheng was a figurehead ruler of the short-lived Da Tianxing kingdom in Yunnan. After the official Yang Ganzhen had the last Da Changhe ruler killed in 928, he placed Zhao on the throne at Yangjumie.

zhao-xie.s: Zhao Xie was a descendant of the old royal house of Zhao, restored as its king during the revolts against the Qin dynasty. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu moved him north to the Kingdom of Dai, giving Zhao to Zhang Er.

zog-i.s: Zog I, born Ahmet Zogu, was an Albanian chieftain from Mat who dominated his country's politics between the wars. He overthrew Fan Noli's government in December 1924, became president of the Albanian Republic in 1925 and proclaimed himself King of the Albanians in 1928.

zhai-zhao.s: Zhai Zhao was the second and last ruler of Zhai Wei, a small Dingling state on the Yellow River during the Sixteen Kingdoms period. He succeeded his father Zhai Liao in 391, but in 392 Murong Chui of the Later Yan forced the river crossing and took his capital Huatai.

zhang-qian.s: Zhang Qian was a Han dynasty envoy sent west by Emperor Wu around 138 BCE to seek an alliance with the Yuezhi against the Xiongnu. Held captive by the Xiongnu for years, he reached Dayuan, Kangju and Bactria and returned in 126 BCE; a later mission went to the Wusun.

zalim-singh-jhala.s: Zalim Singh Jhala was the regent and real ruler of Kota in Rajasthan from the 1770s until his death in 1824. A capable administrator and soldier, he reformed the revenue, kept Kota safe from Maratha and Pindari raids and allied with the British in 1817.

zaporozhian-cossacks.s: The Zaporozhian Cossacks were the Cossacks of the lower Dnieper, organised from the 16th century around the fortified Zaporozhian Sich beyond the river's rapids. Under Bohdan Khmelnytsky they led the rising of 1648 against Poland-Lithuania that created the Cossack Hetmanate.

zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahyan.s: Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1966, when he replaced his brother Shakhbut, and used its new oil revenues for rapid development. With Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum of Dubai he led the talks among the Trucial States that created the United Arab Emirates in…

zhai-liao.s: Zhai Liao was a Dingling chieftain who founded the Zhai Wei state on the Yellow River in Henan during the break-up of the Former Qin. After serving and turning on several powers in turn, he proclaimed himself Heavenly King of Wei in 388.

zhang-bangchang.s: Zhang Bangchang was a Song dynasty chancellor installed by the Jurchen Jin as emperor of the puppet state of Da Chu at Kaifeng in 1127, after they captured the city and deported the Song emperors Huizong and Qinzong. He held the throne for about a month, then handed power back…

zhang-shicheng.s: Zhang Shicheng was a salt-boat worker who rose in revolt against the Yuan dynasty in 1353 and set up the state of Zhou, ruling the rich Yangtze delta from Suzhou. He wavered between rebellion and Yuan allegiance, and his troops killed the Red Turban leader Liu Futong in 1363.

zhang-xianzhong.s: Zhang Xianzhong was a peasant rebel leader of the late Ming dynasty. After years of campaigning across northern and central China, he took Chengdu in 1644 and proclaimed the Great Xi state in Sichuan.

zhang-zuolin.s: Zhang Zuolin was a Chinese warlord who rose from bandit leader to master of Manchuria as head of the Fengtian clique. During the Beiyang period he fought the Zhili clique for control of Beijing and from 1927 headed the Beiyang government himself.

zhao-tuo.s: Zhao Tuo was a Qin general sent to conquer the far south who founded the kingdom of Nanyue, with its capital at Panyu (Guangzhou), in 204 BCE. Ruling Chinese settlers and Yue peoples, he adopted local customs, accepted Han overlordship in 196 BCE and later styled himself emperor.

zheng-jing.s: Zheng Jing was the son of Koxinga and ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning on Taiwan from 1662 to 1681. With his minister Chen Yonghua he built a Chinese-style administration at Tungning (Tainan), founding Taiwan's first Confucian temple and encouraging foreign trade.

zheng-keshuang.s: Zheng Keshuang was the last ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning on Taiwan and a grandson of Koxinga. Court factions placed him on the throne as a boy after his father Zheng Jing died in 1681.

zheng-longdan.s: Zheng Longdan was the last king of Da Changhe, the Zheng family's kingdom in Yunnan that had replaced Nanzhao in 902. He came to the throne young in 926, while rivalry among the great families of the Erhai region weakened the court.

zheng-maisi.s: Zheng Maisi was a minister of Nanzhao, descended from a Tang official captured by the kingdom. In 902 he massacred the Meng royal family and proclaimed the kingdom of Da Changhe, centred on the Erhai basin of Yunnan.

zhenzhu-khagan.s: Zhenzhu Khagan, personal name Yinan, was the leader of the Xueyantuo, a Tiele people of Mongolia. He led their revolt against the Eastern Turkic Khaganate in 628 and was recognised as khagan by Emperor Taizong of Tang.

zhingshak-tseten-dorje.s: Zhingshak Tseten Dorje, also called Karma Tseten, was the founder of the Tsangpa dynasty of Tibet. An official of the Rinpungpa at Samdrubtse (Shigatse), he rebelled in the 1550s and by 1565 had replaced his masters as ruler of Tsang.

zhu-youzhen.s: Zhu Youzhen was the last emperor of the Later Liang dynasty in northern China, a son of its founder Zhu Wen. In 913 he overthrew his brother Zhu Yougui, who had murdered their father.

ziri-ibn-atiyya.s: Ziri ibn Atiyya was a chief of the Maghrawa, a Zenata Berber tribe, and an ally of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba against the Fatimids. Around 987 he took control of Fez as Córdoba's governor, and in 994 he founded Oujda.

zviad-gamsakhurdia.s: Zviad Gamsakhurdia was a Georgian dissident writer and nationalist leader who became the first elected president of Georgia. His coalition won the Soviet Georgian elections of 1990, and Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991, with him elected president the following month.

zeki-velidi-togan.s: Zeki Velidi Togan, born Akhmetzaki Validov, was a Bashkir national leader and historian. In 1917 to 1920 he led the government of autonomous Bashkurdistan, negotiating between the Whites and the Bolsheviks before breaking with Soviet power and joining the Basmachi in Central…

zainal-abidin-of-ternate.s: Zainal Abidin of Ternate was ruler of Ternate in the Maluku Islands in the late fifteenth century. He studied Islam at Giri in eastern Java and is credited with formally adopting Islam and taking the title of sultan, making Ternate the first Islamic sultanate of the Moluccas.

zainal-abidin-i-of-terengganu.s: Zainal Abidin I of Terengganu was the founder of the present Terengganu Sultanate on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula. A son of the Bendahara family of the Johor Sultanate, he became sultan around 1708, and his descendants still rule Terengganu as a state of Malaysia.

zahir-al-umar.s: Zahir al-Umar was an Arab sheikh of the Zaydani clan who built an autonomous domain in Galilee in the 18th century, taking Tiberias and making Acre his capital and a busy cotton-exporting port. He defied the Ottoman governors of Damascus and allied with Ali Bey of Egypt and…

zain-ul-abidin.s: Zain-ul-Abidin, called Budshah, the great king, was sultan of Kashmir from 1418 to 1470 in the Shah Mir dynasty. He reversed his father Sikandar's persecution, allowed Hindu Pandits to return, had Sanskrit works translated into Persian and patronised crafts.

zakhary-chepiha.s: Zakhary Chepiha was a Cossack commander who led the Black Sea Cossack Host formed from former Zaporozhians. He fought in the Russo-Turkish War of 1787 to 1792, including the capture of Izmail.

zakkur.s: Zakkur was an Aramaean king of Hamath and Lu'ash around 800 BCE, probably a usurper. His Aramaic stele, found at Tell Afis, ancient Hatarikka, records how the god Baalshamin saved him when a coalition of kings led by Bar-Hadad of Aram-Damascus besieged him there.

zanticus.s: Zanticus was a king of the Iazyges, a Sarmatian people of the Hungarian plain, during the Marcomannic Wars. After the Romans defeated his people, he made peace with Marcus Aurelius in 175, returning tens of thousands of Roman captives and providing 8,000 cavalry, of whom 5,500…

zasagt-khan.s: Zasagt Khan was the title of the Chinggisid rulers of the western Khalkha Mongols, one of the three, later four, Khalkha khanates. The title was adopted in the late 16th century by a branch of Geresenje's descendants ruling towards the Khangai and Altai mountains.

zawi-ibn-ziri.s: Zawi ibn Ziri was a Sanhaja Berber leader of the Zirid family who came to al-Andalus to serve the Caliphate of Córdoba. During the civil war after 1009 he seized the district of Elvira around 1013 and moved its centre to Granada, founding the Taifa of Granada.

zayed-bin-khalifa-al-nahyan.s: Zayed bin Khalifa Al Nahyan, known as Zayed the Great, was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1855 to 1909. Through war and alliances with inland tribes he made Abu Dhabi the strongest of the Trucial States, and he signed the Exclusive Agreement with Britain in 1892.

zayyan-ibn-mardanish.s: Zayyan ibn Mardanish was the last Muslim ruler of Valencia, a descendant of Muhammad ibn Mardanish, the Wolf King. In 1229 he overthrew the Almohad governor Abu Zayd and took Valencia, but James I of Aragon conquered the kingdom, winning at Puig in 1237 and taking the city…

zenobia.s: Zenobia was queen of Palmyra, who ruled for her young son Vaballathus after the murder of her husband Odaenathus in 267. She conquered Egypt in 270 and much of Anatolia, creating a breakaway Palmyrene Empire in Rome's East.

zeus-polieus.s: Zeus Polieus, Zeus of the city, was a form of the Greek god Zeus worshipped as protector of a city and its citizens. His cult was often shared with Athena Polias on the acropolis, as at Athens, where the Dipolieia festival honoured him.

zhang-fu-ming-general.s: Zhang Fu was a Ming general who served in the 1406 to 1407 invasion of Vietnam that overthrew the Ho dynasty and created Jiaozhi province. He returned several times to crush resistance, capturing the Later Tran rulers Gian Dinh in 1409 and Trung Quang in 1414.

zhang-gui.s: Zhang Gui was a Chinese official appointed governor of Liang province in the far north-west by the Western Jin in 301. Ruling from Guzang, he restored order, encouraged learning and welcomed refugees from the wars in northern China.

zhang-jun-former-liang.s: Zhang Jun was ruler of Former Liang from 324 to 346, a grandson of its founder Zhang Gui. Under him the state reached its greatest extent, controlling the Hexi Corridor and influence in the Western Regions, and in 327 he established Gaochang commandery in the Turpan basin.

zhang-tianxi.s: Zhang Tianxi was the last ruler of Former Liang, who seized power in 363. In 376 the Former Qin ruler Fu Jian invaded, and Zhang Tianxi surrendered and served at the Qin court.

zhang-yichao.s: Zhang Yichao was a local leader of Dunhuang who in 848 drove out the Tibetan garrison as the Tibetan Empire disintegrated, and went on to free other towns of the Hexi Corridor. The Tang court recognised him in 851 as military governor of the Guiyi Circuit.

zhao-mo.s: Zhao Mo was the second king of Nanyue, grandson of its founder Zhao Tuo, reigning from 137 BCE. He relied on the Han dynasty for help against Minyue.

zhao-xiangzi.s: Zhao Xiangzi was head of the Zhao lineage, ministers of the State of Jin, in the 5th century BCE. Around 457 BCE he killed the king of Dai at a banquet and annexed his state.

zhelyu-zhelev.s: Zhelyu Zhelev was a Bulgarian philosopher and dissident whose book on fascism was banned under communism. He led the opposition Union of Democratic Forces in 1989 and 1990, was elected president by parliament in 1990 and became the first directly elected president of Bulgaria…

zhu-yougui.s: Zhu Yougui was the second emperor of the Later Liang in the Five Dynasties period. In 912 he murdered his father Zhu Wen, the dynasty's founder, and took the throne.

zhuge-liang.s: Zhuge Liang was the chancellor of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period and chief adviser to Liu Bei, whose alliance with Sun Quan led to victory at Red Cliffs in 208. After Liu Bei's death he governed for Liu Shan, pacified the south and led five northern expeditions against…

ziaur-rahman.s: Ziaur Rahman was a Bangladeshi army officer who announced the declaration of independence on radio in March 1971 and commanded forces in the Liberation War. After the coups of 1975 he became the country's leading figure and was president from 1977.

zmitser-zhylunovich.s: Zmitser Zhylunovich was a Belarusian writer, known by the pen name Tsishka Hartny, and head of the provisional government of the Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia proclaimed in January 1919. He broke with the Bolsheviks when the republic was merged into the…

zorawar-singh.s: Zorawar Singh was a Dogra general in the service of Gulab Singh of Jammu. Between 1834 and 1840 he conquered Ladakh and Baltistan, bringing them into the Dogra realm that later became the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.

zou-yao.s: Zou Yao was a descendant of King Goujian of Yue who helped the Han against Xiang Yu. In 192 BCE Emperor Hui of Han made him King of Donghai, ruling from Dong'ou in southern Zhejiang.

zulfikar-ali-bhutto.s: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was a Pakistani statesman who founded the Pakistan Peoples Party in 1967. After the loss of East Pakistan in 1971 he became president and then prime minister, nationalised industries, introduced the 1973 constitution and began Pakistan's nuclear programme.

zahir-al-din-marashi.s: Zahir al-Din Mar'ashi was a Persian historian of the 15th century from the Mar'ashi family of sayyids who ruled Mazandaran. He wrote histories of Tabaristan, Ruyan and Mazandaran and of Gilan, which are the main sources for the local dynasties of the Caspian provinces of Iran…

ziyadat-allah-i.s: Ziyadat Allah I was the Aghlabid emir of Ifriqiya from 817 to 838. After surviving a long revolt of the Arab army, he sent a fleet under the jurist Asad ibn al-Furat to invade Byzantine Sicily in 827, beginning a conquest that took about seventy-five years.

ziyadat-allah-iii.s: Ziyadat Allah III was the last Aghlabid emir of Ifriqiya, who came to power in 903 after having his father, Abdallah II, murdered. He could not stop the advance of the Kutama Berbers under the Fatimid missionary Abu Abdallah al-Shi'i, and in 909 he fled east with his treasure.

zaydism.s: Zaydism is a branch of Shia Islam named after Zayd ibn Ali, a great-grandson of the caliph Ali, who led a revolt against the Umayyads in 740. Zaydis accept as imam any qualified descendant of Hasan or Husayn who claims the office and takes up arms, and they stand close to…

zagora-andros.s: Zagora is an archaeological site on a headland on the west coast of Andros in the Cyclades, Greece. It was a fortified town of the Geometric period, flourishing in the 8th century BCE and abandoned around 700 BCE.

zafiraminia.s: The Zafiraminia were a ruling clan of south-eastern Madagascar who claimed descent from Muslim immigrants, traditionally from Arabia. From around 1500 they formed the aristocracy of the Antanosy, keeping Arabic-script writing (sorabe) and ritual privileges such as the…

zinciriye-madrasa.s: The Zinciriye Madrasa, also known as the Sultan Isa Madrasa, is a medieval madrasa in Mardin in south-eastern Turkey, completed in 1385 under the Artuqid ruler Sultan Isa. Built of the local golden stone on the hillside above the city, it has a richly carved portal, domed…

zeami-motokiyo.s: Zeami Motokiyo was a Japanese actor, playwright and theorist who, with his father Kan'ami, created Noh theatre in its classic form. Patronised as a youth by the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, he wrote many of the plays still performed and treatises on acting that stress yūgen, a…

zadar.s: Zadar is a city on the Adriatic coast of Croatia, known in Italian as Zara. A Roman colony as Iader, it was later a leading Dalmatian city contested between Venice and Hungary, and the Fourth Crusade sacked it for Venice in 1202.

zangezur.s: Zangezur is a mountainous region of the South Caucasus, largely matching Armenia's Syunik province, between Nakhchivan and Karabakh. After the Russian Empire collapsed it was contested by Armenia and Azerbaijan, and in 1920–1921 Garegin Nzhdeh held it against Soviet forces as…

zeerust.s: Zeerust is a town in the Marico district of South Africa's North West province, near the border with Botswana. It was founded in 1867 by settlers of the South African Republic on the farm of Casper Coetzee.

zell-e-soltan.s: Zell-e Soltan, born Mas'ud Mirza, was the eldest son of the Qajar ruler Naser al-Din Shah, excluded from the succession because his mother was not of royal birth. As governor of Isfahan from 1874 he ruled much of southern and central Iran, building a strong army and a large…

zalavar.s: Zalavár is a village in Zala county in western Hungary, near the south-western end of Lake Balaton. In the 9th century, as Mosapurc or Mosaburg, it was the fortified seat of the Slavic princes Pribina and Kocel under Frankish overlordship, built on an island in the marshes of…

zala-river.s: The Zala is a river in western Hungary which rises near the Austrian border and flows east and then south to empty into Lake Balaton near Keszthely, as the lake's main tributary. Its marshy lower valley sheltered the 9th-century fortress of Mosapurc, now Zalavár, seat of the…

zubarah.s: Zubarah is a ruined town on the north-west coast of Qatar. Settled in the 18th century by clans of the Bani Utbah, including the Al Khalifa, it grew into a thriving centre of pearling and trade, and in 1783 the Al Khalifa crossed from there to take Bahrain.

zawila.s: Zawila is an oasis town in the Fezzan region of south-western Libya, east of Murzuq. In the early Islamic period it was the chief town of the Fezzan and a major station on the caravan route between Lake Chad and the Mediterranean, through which enslaved people were brought north.

zarubintsy-culture.s: The Zarubintsy culture was an Iron Age archaeological culture of the middle and upper Dnieper basin, in modern Ukraine and Belarus, from about the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE. It is known from unfortified settlements and cremation cemeteries.

zayn-al-din-ali-kuchuk.s: Zayn al-Din Ali Kuchuk, son of Begtegin, was a Turkmen officer of the Zengid ruler Imad al-Din Zengi. From around 1144 he governed Erbil and other towns in northern Iraq and became the most powerful lord of the Zengid state of Mosul.

zana-malata.s: The Zana-malata were the descendants of European and American pirates and Malagasy women on the north-east coast of Madagascar, where many pirates settled around 1700. In the 18th century they formed an influential elite among the Betsimisaraka.

zavist.s: Závist is a Celtic hillfort on a hill above the Vltava just south of Prague in the Czech Republic. A sanctuary and fortified centre in the Hallstatt period, it became one of the largest oppida of the Boii in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE, defended by long ramparts and gates.

zunyi.s: Zunyi is a city in northern Guizhou province in south-western China. It grew around Bozhou, the domain ruled by the hereditary Yang chieftains from the 9th century until the Ming conquest in 1600.

zomba.s: Zomba is a city in southern Malawi, below the Zomba Plateau in the Shire Highlands. Chosen by Harry Johnston as the headquarters of the British Central Africa Protectorate in 1891, it remained the capital of Nyasaland and of independent Malawi until the government moved to…

zollfeld.s: The Zollfeld is a plain in the valley of the Glan, north of Klagenfurt in the Austrian state of Carinthia. It was the site of the Roman city of Virunum, capital of the province of Noricum, and later the centre of Slavic Carantania.

zulfiqar-khan.s: Zulfiqar Khan was a Mughal general and statesman who commanded Aurangzeb's armies in southern India and was appointed the first Nawab of the Carnatic in 1692. He took the Maratha fortress of Gingee in 1698.

zamorin.s: The Zamorin, in Malayalam Samoothiri, was the title of the Hindu rulers of the Kingdom of Calicut on the Malabar Coast of Kerala from about the 12th century to 1766. Growing rich on the spice trade with Arab and other Muslim merchants, the Zamorins received Vasco da Gama in…

zygii.s: The Zygii, or Zygoi, were a people of the north-eastern Black Sea coast mentioned by Greek and Roman geographers such as Strabo, who described them as pirates. Generally seen as ancestors of the Circassians, they gave their name to the medieval land of Zichia, where Byzantine…

zarbienus.s: Zarbienus was a king of Gordyene (Corduene), in the mountains south of Lake Van, in the 1st century BCE, while it was subject to Tigranes the Great of Armenia. According to Plutarch, he negotiated secretly with the Romans under Lucullus, was betrayed and put to death with his…

zurichgau.s: The Zürichgau was an early medieval district (Gau) of Alemannia, covering the land around Lake Zürich and the Limmat between the Reuss and the Thurgau. Recorded from the Carolingian period, it was later divided among lordships held by families such as the counts of Lenzburg,…

zeil-castle.s: Zeil Castle (Schloss Zeil) is a Renaissance castle on a hill near Leutkirch im Allgäu, in Upper Swabia, Germany. Built in the late 16th and early 17th centuries on the site of an older fortress, it is the seat of the princes of Waldburg-Zeil, one of the main branches of the…

zierikzee.s: Zierikzee is a historic town on the island of Schouwen-Duiveland in the Dutch province of Zeeland. It was a flourishing medieval port trading in salt, madder and fish, but declined as its harbour silted up.

zuiderzee.s: The Zuiderzee was a shallow inlet of the North Sea in the north-west Netherlands, enlarged by storm floods in the Middle Ages. Ports such as Kampen, Harderwijk, Enkhuizen and Hoorn traded across it.

zakynthos.s: Zakynthos (Zante) is the southernmost of the main Ionian Islands, off the west coast of the Peloponnese. Taken from Byzantium by the Normans of Sicily in 1185, it was ruled with Cephalonia by counts palatine, came under Venice in 1485 and grew so prosperous that it was called…

zwaanendael.s: Zwaanendael was a Dutch whaling and farming settlement founded in 1631 near modern Lewes, Delaware, by patroons of the Dutch West India Company. Within about a year a quarrel with the local Lenape led to its destruction and the killing of all its settlers.

zhuang-qiao.s: Zhuang Qiao was a general of the state of Chu who, according to the historian Sima Qian, led an army to the Lake Dian region of present-day Yunnan in the 3rd century BCE. When Qin conquests cut his route home, he stayed, adopted local dress and customs and made himself king of…

zotto.s: Zotto was the first Lombard duke of Benevento, establishing himself there around 571 at the head of a Lombard war band, possibly after serving as a mercenary in Byzantine pay. He extended Lombard control over much of inland southern Italy, and his warriors are said to have…

znojmo.s: Znojmo is a town in southern Moravia, Czech Republic, on the Thaya river near the Austrian border. From about 1092 it was the seat of a Přemyslid appanage duchy, and the rotunda in its castle preserves 12th-century wall paintings showing rulers of the dynasty.

zagan.s: Żagań is a town on the Bóbr river in western Poland, in historic Lower Silesia. It became the seat of a Piast duchy in the late 13th century, was sold to the Saxon Wettins in 1472 and was later held by Albrecht von Wallenstein, who began its great baroque palace.

ziemomysl-of-inowroclaw.s: Ziemomysł of Inowrocław (c. 1245–1287) was a Polish prince of the Piast dynasty, a son of Casimir I of Kuyavia.

zolta.s: Zolta, or Zoltán, was a Hungarian grand prince of the 10th century, the youngest son of Árpád. According to the Gesta Hungarorum he married the daughter of Menumorut and inherited his lands around Bihar.

zbigniew-olesnicki.s: Zbigniew Oleśnicki was Bishop of Kraków from 1423 to 1455 and the first Polish cardinal. A royal secretary who reportedly saved King Władysław II Jagiełło's life at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410, he became the most powerful statesman in Poland during the minority of Władysław…

ziebice.s: Ziębice (German Münsterberg) is a town in Lower Silesia, Poland, south of Wrocław. From 1322 it was the seat of a Piast duchy and later passed to George of Poděbrady, whose sons held it as dukes of Münsterberg, and from 1654 to the Auersperg family.

zeta-region.s: Zeta is a historical region of present-day Montenegro, named after the Zeta river and its plain around Podgorica. It was the medieval successor of Duklja, a Nemanjić appanage from the late twelfth century, and was ruled by the Balšić and then the Crnojević families from the…

zayn-al-din-karaja.s: Zayn al-Din Karaja was a Turkmen chief who founded the Dulkadirid beylik. In 1337 the Mamluk sultan recognised him as ruler of Elbistan and the uplands of the eastern Taurus, as a vassal guarding the Mamluk northern frontier.

zhu-ying.s: Zhu Ying was an official of Eastern Wu who travelled with Kang Tai on an embassy sent by Sun Quan to Funan, in mainland South-East Asia, in the mid-3rd century. He wrote an account of the country and its neighbours, now lost but cited in later Chinese works, which with Kang…

zwinger-dresden.s: The Zwinger is a Baroque palace complex in Dresden, built from 1710 to 1728 for Augustus the Strong, Elector of Saxony and King of Poland, by the architect Matthäus Daniel Pöppelmann and the sculptor Balthasar Permoser. Designed as a festival arena with galleries and pavilions…

zawaya.s: The Zawaya are the scholarly and religious tribes of Moorish society in Mauritania and the western Sahara, mostly of Sanhaja Berber origin. Unlike the Hassani warrior tribes, they devoted themselves to Islamic learning, teaching, trade and herding.

ziryab.s: Ziryab, born Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Nafi, was a musician and singer from Baghdad who settled at the court of Abd al-Rahman II in Córdoba in 822. Later tradition credits him with introducing eastern fashions in music, dress, hairstyles, cuisine and table manners to al-Andalus,…

zhang-mao.s: Zhang Mao was the ruler of the Former Liang state in the Hexi Corridor of north-western China from 320 to 324. He succeeded his brother Zhang Shi after his assassination, and the state's independent existence is conventionally dated from his accession.

zhengtong-emperor.s: The Zhengtong Emperor, Zhu Qizhen, ruled Ming China from 1435 to 1449 and again, as the Tianshun Emperor, from 1457 to 1464. Urged by the eunuch Wang Zhen, he led a campaign against the Oirats in 1449 and was captured by Esen at the Tumu Fortress.

zell-am-harmersbach.s: Zell am Harmersbach is a small town in the Black Forest in Baden-Württemberg, near Gengenbach. Recognised as a free imperial city in the 14th century, it was one of the smallest imperial estates, with only a few hundred inhabitants, until it passed to Baden in 1803.

zwin.s: The Zwin is a former tidal inlet of the North Sea on the border of Belgium and the Netherlands. Widened by storm floods in the 12th century, it gave Bruges access to the sea through the outports of Damme and Sluis and made it a leading medieval trading city; the Battle of…

zhangye.s: Zhangye is a city in the Hexi Corridor of Gansu province, China. Known in the past as Ganzhou, it was a garrison and trading town on the Silk Road.

zollverein.s: The Zollverein was the customs union of German states led by Prussia, which came into force on 1 January 1834. It abolished tariffs between its members and set a common external tariff, eventually covering most of Germany but excluding Austria.

zalmoxis.s: Zalmoxis was a god or deified teacher of the Getae and Dacians north of the Danube. Herodotus reports that the Getae believed they did not die but went to Zalmoxis, and that every four years they sent him a messenger by throwing a man onto spears.

zhanjiang.s: Zhanjiang is a port city in south-western Guangdong province, China, on the Leizhou Peninsula. It grew from the French leased territory of Guangzhouwan, whose seat was named Fort-Bayard; the territory was returned to China in 1945 and the city took its present name.

zafar-yemen.s: Zafar was the capital of the Himyarite Kingdom in the highlands of south-western Arabia, south of Sanaa in modern Yemen. From the late 1st century BCE until the 6th century CE its kings, styled kings of Saba and Dhu Raydan, ruled from the palace of Raydan there.

zwiefalten.s: Zwiefalten is a municipality in the district of Reutlingen in the Swabian Jura, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It grew around a Benedictine abbey founded in 1089 by the counts of Achalm and settled from Hirsau, which became an imperial abbey in 1750.

zenodorus.s: Zenodorus was an Ituraean ruler of the 1st century BCE who leased the lands of Lysanias, including Trachonitis, Auranitis and Batanaea. Accused of tolerating brigands, he lost these territories when Augustus gave them to Herod the Great in 23 BCE, and on his death in 20 BCE…

zhongdu.s: Zhongdu, the Central Capital, was the main capital of the Jurchen Jin dynasty from 1153 to 1215, on the site of south-western Beijing. Enlarged from the earlier Liao city by Wanyan Liang, it had grand palaces and walls.

zhetiru.s: The Zhetiru, meaning "seven clans", are one of the three tribal groupings of the Junior Zhuz, the western branch of the Kazakh people. Formed as a union of seven smaller clans, they lived in the north-western steppes of Kazakhstan, along the Russian frontier line.

zen.s: Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism that stresses meditation and direct insight over scripture. It arose in China as Chan, spread to Korea as Seon and was brought to Japan by Eisai and Dogen in the late 12th and 13th centuries.

zhety-zhargy.s: The Zhety Zhargy ('Seven Charters') is a code of customary law of the Kazakh Khanate, traditionally attributed to Tauke Khan in the late 17th century and to the leading judges (biys) of the three Kazakh hordes. It dealt with land, family, crime, blood money and relations…

zamboanga-del-norte.s: Zamboanga del Norte is a province on the north-western coast of Mindanao in the Philippines, with its capital at Dipolog. It includes the historic town of Dapitan, where the national hero José Rizal lived in exile from 1892 to 1896.

zhou-qufei.s: Zhou Qufei was a Chinese scholar-official of the Southern Song dynasty who served in Guangxi. In 1178 he completed the Lingwai Daida ('Notes from the Land beyond the Passes'), which describes southern China and foreign lands reached by sea, from South-East Asia to the Arab world.

zuhayr-ibn-qays.s: Zuhayr ibn Qays al-Balawi was an Arab commander sent by the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik to recover Ifriqiya after the death of Uqba ibn Nafi. In the late 680s he defeated the Berber leader Kusaila, who was killed in the battle, and retook Kairouan.

zuhayr-of-almeria.s: Zuhayr was a freedman of the Amirid household, of Slavic (Saqaliba) origin, who ruled the taifa of Almería in al-Andalus from about 1028, succeeding his fellow freedman Khayran. His rivalry with the Zirid rulers of Granada led to war, and he was killed in battle against Badis…

zipoetes-i-of-bithynia.s: Zipoetes I was a ruler of Bithynia in north-western Anatolia who successfully resisted the Hellenistic kings Lysimachus and Seleucus I. Ruling from about 326 BCE as a local dynast, he took the title of king in 297 BCE, founding the Bithynian royal dynasty and the era by which…

zulpich.s: Zülpich is a town in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, west of Bonn, on the site of the Roman settlement of Tolbiacum. It is associated with the battle in which the Franks defeated the Alemanni around 496, traditionally linked with the conversion of Clovis I, and Sigibert of…

zagreb.s: Zagreb is the capital and largest city of Croatia, on the Sava river. It grew from two medieval settlements, the bishop's Kaptol, seat of a bishopric founded in 1094, and the royal free town of Gradec, which were united in 1850.

zango.s: Zango is a town in Katsina State, northern Nigeria, east of Daura. After the Fulani jihad took Daura in the early 19th century, the old Hausa dynasty of Daura ruled from exile at Zango, and after 1903 the British restored the head of the Zango line as emir of Daura, whose…

zhao-erfeng.s: Zhao Erfeng was a Qing official and general who imposed direct Chinese rule on Kham, eastern Tibet, from 1905. He abolished local kingdoms and chieftaincies, including Derge in 1909, and his campaigns prepared the Qing army's entry into Lhasa in 1910.

zakarids.s: The Zakarids, or Mkhargrdzeli, were an Armenian noble family who served the kings of Georgia as commanders. Under Queen Tamar the brothers Zakare and Ivane took Ani in 1199 and much of Armenia from the Shaddadids and Seljuks, ruling it as Georgian vassals.

zedekiah.s: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon in 597 BCE. When he rebelled with Egyptian encouragement, the Babylonians besieged Jerusalem, which fell in 587 or 586 BCE.

zeno-of-citium.s: Zeno of Citium was a philosopher from Kition in Cyprus who founded Stoicism. Arriving in Athens around 312 BCE, he studied with the Cynic Crates and others, and from about 300 BCE taught in the Stoa Poikile, the painted colonnade that gave the school its name.

zeno-of-elea.s: Zeno of Elea was a Greek philosopher of the Eleatic school and a pupil of Parmenides. He is famous for his paradoxes, such as Achilles and the tortoise and the flying arrow, which argued that motion and plurality lead to contradictions and so defended Parmenides' view that…

zeno-emperor.s: Zeno was Eastern Roman emperor from 474 to 491, with a break in 475–476 when he was driven out by the usurper Basiliscus. An Isaurian general who married the daughter of Leo I, he received the imperial regalia from Odoacer after the end of the Western empire in 476 and later…

zwentibold.s: Zwentibold was the illegitimate son of the East Frankish king Arnulf of Carinthia, who made him king of Lotharingia in 895. His rule provoked the Lotharingian nobility, led by Reginar, and after Arnulf's death he was killed in battle on the Meuse on 13 August 900.

zimba.s: The Zimba were warrior bands from the Zambezi region who appear in Portuguese sources of the late 16th century. They attacked Portuguese posts on the Zambezi and in 1587–1589 marched up the East African coast, sacking Kilwa and reaching Mombasa, before being defeated near…

zdzislaw-lubomirski.s: Zdzisław Lubomirski was a Polish aristocrat and politician, mayor of Warsaw from 1916 to 1917. He was a member of the Regency Council that governed the Kingdom of Poland under German and Austrian occupation in 1917–18 and transferred power to Józef Piłsudski in November 1918.

zheng-zhilong.s: Zheng Zhilong was a Chinese merchant and pirate who built a great maritime trading network from Fujian, Japan and Taiwan. He entered Ming service as an admiral, supported the Ming loyalist court in Fujian, then surrendered to the Qing in 1646.

zamfara-state.s: Zamfara State is a state in north-western Nigeria, created in 1996 from part of Sokoto State, with its capital at Gusau. It takes its name from the Hausa kingdom of Zamfara, which flourished before the Fulani jihad of the early 19th century.

zababa.s: Zababa was a Mesopotamian god of war and the patron deity of the city of Kish. His temple there was called E-mete-ursag, and his consort was the goddess Bau or, in later times, Inanna, who also had a temple at Kish.

zacpeten.s: Zacpetén is a Maya archaeological site on a peninsula in Lake Salpetén in the Petén department of northern Guatemala. Occupied from the Preclassic period, it became an important centre of the Kowoj Maya in the Postclassic, before the Spanish conquest of Petén in 1697.

zappo-zap.s: The Zappo Zap were a Songye group from the Kasai region of the Congo, named after their leader Zappo Zap, who settled near Luluabourg in the 1880s and became auxiliaries of the Congo Free State. Armed with firearms, they collected taxes, rubber and slaves for the state, and in…

zu-chongzhi.s: Zu Chongzhi was a Chinese mathematician and astronomer of the Liu Song and Southern Qi dynasties. He calculated pi to lie between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, a precision not surpassed for nearly a thousand years, and gave 355/113 as a close approximation.

zaleucus.s: Zaleucus was the lawgiver of Locri Epizephyrii in southern Italy, credited with drawing up the first written Greek law code in the mid-7th century BCE. His laws fixed penalties in advance rather than leaving them to the judges, and were known for their severity.

zulju.s: Zulju (Dulucha) was a Mongol or Turkic commander who invaded Kashmir in 1320 with a large army, plundering, burning and enslaving across the valley for about eight months. King Suhadeva fled, and the devastation allowed the Ladakhi prince Rinchan to seize power; the Lohara…

zwolle.s: Zwolle is a city in the north-eastern Netherlands, capital of the province of Overijssel. A Hanseatic town near the IJssel, it prospered on river trade in the late Middle Ages and was a centre of the Devotio Moderna; Thomas à Kempis lived at the nearby monastery of Mount Saint…

zaccaria.s: The Zaccaria were a Genoese merchant family who built an Aegean domain in the late 13th and 14th centuries. Benedetto Zaccaria received the alum mines of Phocaea from the Byzantines and occupied Chios in 1304, which the family held until 1329.

zwickauer-mulde.s: The Zwickauer Mulde is a river in Saxony, Germany, about 165 kilometres long. It rises in the Vogtland near the Czech border and flows north past Aue, Zwickau, Glauchau and Waldenburg, joining the Freiberger Mulde near Grimma to form the Mulde, a tributary of the Elbe.

zhu-fan-zhi.s: The Zhu Fan Zhi ('Records of Foreign Peoples') is a Chinese work completed around 1225 by Zhao Rugua, a Song dynasty superintendent of maritime trade at Quanzhou. Based on interviews with merchants and sailors, it describes the countries, peoples and goods of Southeast Asia,…

zheng-xiaoxu.s: Zheng Xiaoxu was a Chinese official, poet and calligrapher who served the Qing dynasty and remained loyal to the deposed emperor Puyi after 1912. He helped bring Puyi to Manchuria and became the first prime minister of Manchukuo in 1932.

zhang-jinghui.s: Zhang Jinghui was a Chinese general of the Fengtian clique in Manchuria who served the Japanese-backed state of Manchukuo. He succeeded Zheng Xiaoxu as prime minister in 1935 and held the post until the state collapsed in 1945, while Japanese officials and the Kwantung Army…

zoroaster.s: Zoroaster was the prophet of ancient Iran whose hymns, the Gathas, stand at the origin of Zoroastrianism, among the world's oldest revealed religions. His dates are disputed by a thousand years, with most scholars now favouring the late second millennium BCE.

ziwiye.s: Ziwiye is a hilltop fortress site near Saqqez in Kurdistan province, Iran. In 1947 local people found there a hoard of gold, silver and ivory objects of the 7th century BCE, mixing Assyrian, Urartian, Scythian and local styles, which was scattered among dealers and museums.

zeitz.s: Zeitz is a town on the White Elster river in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Otto I made it the seat of a bishopric in 968, which moved to Naumburg in the 11th century.

zittau.s: Zittau is a town in the south-east of Saxony, Germany, near the borders with Poland and the Czech Republic. A wealthy cloth-trading town under the Bohemian crown, it was a founding member of the Six Towns League of Upper Lusatia in 1346.

zhangjiakou.s: Zhangjiakou, formerly known as Kalgan, is a city in north-western Hebei province, China, at a gateway through the Great Wall towards Mongolia. It long served as a trading centre between China, Mongolia and Russia, especially for tea caravans.

zapatista-army-of-national-liberation.s: The Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN) is a mainly indigenous revolutionary movement in Chiapas, southern Mexico, named after the revolutionary Emiliano Zapata. On 1 January 1994, the day NAFTA came into force, it seized several towns in the state, demanding land,…

zou-wuzhu.s: Zou Wuzhu was the first king of Minyue, the kingdom of the Min Yue people in present-day Fujian. Claiming descent from King Goujian of Yue, he had been demoted under the Qin dynasty but supported Liu Bang against Xiang Yu, and in 202 BCE the new Han dynasty recognised him as…

zou-ying.s: Zou Ying was a king of Minyue in present-day Fujian in the 2nd century BCE. He pursued an aggressive policy against neighbouring Yue kingdoms, attacking Dong'ou in 138 BCE and Nanyue in 135 BCE.

zou-yushan.s: Zou Yushan was a prince of the Minyue royal house in present-day Fujian. In 135 BCE he killed his brother King Zou Ying to avert a Han invasion and was then made king of Dongyue by the Han.

zered.s: The Zered, now Wadi al-Hasa, is a river valley in Jordan that runs west into the southern end of the Dead Sea. In antiquity it formed the boundary between Moab to the north and Edom to the south, and the Hebrew Bible records that the Israelites crossed it on their journey to…

zograf-monastery.s: Zograf Monastery is the Bulgarian monastery of Mount Athos in northern Greece, traditionally founded in the late 10th century and dedicated to Saint George. Its name, 'the painter', comes from a legend of an icon that painted itself.

zapotec-civilization.s: The Zapotec civilization arose in the Valley of Oaxaca in southern Mexico, where from about 500 BCE Monte Albán became one of the first cities and states of Mesoamerica. The Zapotecs developed one of the earliest writing systems in the Americas, built temple and palace…

zelaya-department.s: Zelaya Department was the large department of eastern Nicaragua formed from the former Mosquito Reserve after its forcible incorporation in 1894, and named after President José Santos Zelaya. It covered the whole Caribbean coast, home to Miskito, Creole and other communities.

zwide.s: Zwide was king of the Ndwandwe in present-day northern KwaZulu-Natal in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. He killed the Mthethwa leader Dingiswayo in about 1818 and then fought Shaka's Zulu, who defeated him at the Mhlatuze River in 1819.

zipaquira.s: Zipaquirá is a town north of Bogotá in Cundinamarca, Colombia, built over large rock-salt deposits. Under the Muisca it was a major source of salt, a staple of their trade, and the Spanish continued to exploit its mines.

zibhebhu-kamaphitha.s: Zibhebhu kaMaphitha was a Zulu chief of the Mandlakazi, a branch of the royal house, who fought in the Anglo-Zulu War of 1879. In the British settlement that followed he became one of thirteen chiefs ruling Zululand and the main rival of Cetshwayo and his heir Dinuzulu.

zeus.s: Zeus was the chief god of the ancient Greek pantheon, ruler of the sky and of the Olympian gods, and guardian of oaths, hospitality and kingship. His great sanctuaries included Olympia, where the Olympic Games were held in his honour, and the oracle at Dodona in Epirus.

zopyrion.s: Zopyrion was a Macedonian general whom Alexander the Great left as governor of Thrace. Probably around 331 BCE he led a large army against the Getae and Scythians and besieged the Greek city of Olbia on the Black Sea.

zeugitana.s: Zeugitana was the northern region of Roman Africa, around Carthage, in what is now northern Tunisia. The name was used for the old core of the province of Africa Proconsularis after Diocletian's reforms around 303 separated Byzacena and Tripolitania.

zenko.s: Zenkō was a prince of Baekje, son of King Uija, who lived in Japan as a hostage and stayed there after Baekje fell in 660. The Japanese court gave his family the surname Kudara no Konikishi, meaning king of Baekje, and they became a noble house.

ziyarid-dynasty.s: The Ziyarid dynasty was an Iranian dynasty of Gilaki origin founded by Mardavij ibn Ziyar, which ruled Tabaristan and Gurgan on the southern shore of the Caspian Sea. After Mardavij's brief conquest of much of western Iran, his successors were confined to the Caspian…

zakar-baal.s: Zakar-Baal was a king of Byblos around 1075 BCE, known from the Egyptian Story of Wenamun. When the envoy Wenamun arrived to obtain cedar for the barque of Amun, Zakar-Baal demanded payment, consulted his ancestors' records of earlier transactions and treated Egypt as a…

zurich-bible.s: The Zürich Bible is the German translation of the Bible produced by Huldrych Zwingli, Leo Jud and their colleagues of the Prophezei in Zürich. Printed by Christoph Froschauer and completed in 1531, three years before Luther's complete Bible, it made use of Luther's New…

zurich-oberland.s: The Zürich Oberland is the hilly eastern part of the canton of Zürich, around the towns of Wetzikon, Hinwil and Bauma. From the seventeenth century its households spun and wove cotton and silk for city merchants, and in the nineteenth century water-powered factories spread…

zeelandic-flanders.s: Zeelandic Flanders is the southernmost part of the Dutch province of Zeeland, a strip of land between the Western Scheldt and the Belgian border. Once part of the County of Flanders, it was conquered by the forces of the Dutch Republic during the Eighty Years' War, and the…

zincirli-medrese.s: The Zincirli Medrese is an Islamic college built in 1500 by Khan Meñli I Giray at Salaçıq, near Bakhchysarai in Crimea, beside his family mausoleum. Named after the chain (zincir) hung over its gateway, which obliged everyone entering to bow, it was a leading centre of…

zb-vz-26.s: The ZB vz. 26 was a light machine gun designed by Václav Holek at the Zbrojovka Brno arms works and adopted by the Czechoslovak army in 1926.

zlin.s: Zlín is a city in eastern Moravia in the Czech Republic. From the 1890s it grew from a small town into an industrial centre as the home of the Bata shoe company, which rebuilt it in a modernist style with brick factories and workers' housing.

zaya-pandita.s: Zaya Pandita Namkhai Gyatso was an Oirat Buddhist monk and scholar who studied in Tibet and returned to the western Mongols in 1639 as a missionary. In 1648 he created the Clear script, an adaptation of the Mongolian alphabet that recorded Oirat speech more precisely, and with…

zhi-dun.s: Zhi Dun was a Buddhist monk and scholar of the Eastern Jin dynasty who moved in the aristocratic circles of Jiankang and the south-east. He interpreted Buddhist ideas such as emptiness in the language of Daoist 'dark learning' and was admired for his skill in 'pure…

zacharias-ursinus.s: Zacharias Ursinus was a German Reformed theologian, born in Breslau and a pupil of Philip Melanchthon at Wittenberg. Called to Heidelberg in 1561 under Elector Frederick III, he was the principal author of the Heidelberg Catechism of 1563.

zahara-de-la-sierra.s: Zahara de la Sierra is a village in the province of Cádiz, Spain, crowned by a Moorish castle above the Guadalete valley. A frontier fortress between Castile and the Nasrid Emirate of Granada, it was taken by Castile in 1407 and recaptured by the emir Abu al-Hasan Ali in…

zouaves.s: The Zouaves were light infantry regiments of the French Army, first raised in Algeria in 1830 and named after the Zwawa, a Kabyle tribal confederation that supplied the earliest recruits. Later recruited mainly from European settlers and Frenchmen, they were famed for their…

zhangsun-sheng.s: Zhangsun Sheng was a Chinese general and diplomat of the Northern Zhou and Sui dynasties who specialised in relations with the Turks. Having lived at the Turkic court, he advised the Sui founder Emperor Wen to divide the khaganate by backing rival khans, summed up as…

zhengdong-province.s: Zhengdong Province, the Branch Secretariat for the Eastern Campaign, was an office set up by the Yuan dynasty in Goryeo in 1280 to prepare the invasion of Japan. It was kept after the campaign as an instrument of Yuan supervision, with the Goryeo king nominally at its head.

zhang-congzheng.s: Zhang Congzheng was a physician of the Jin dynasty and one of the four great medical masters of the Jin and Yuan periods. He held that illness was caused by harmful influences entering the body, and that these should be driven out by sweating, vomiting and purging, founding…

zhou-daguan.s: Zhou Daguan was a Chinese official of the Yuan dynasty who accompanied an embassy sent by Temür Khan to Angkor in 1296–1297. His account of the visit, A Record of Cambodia, describes the city, its temples, royal processions, trade, customs and daily life.

zechariah-of-israel.s: Zechariah was king of Israel for six months around 753 BCE, the son of Jeroboam II and the last ruler of the dynasty of Jehu. According to the Bible he was murdered in public by Shallum, who took the throne.

zimri-king-of-israel.s: Zimri was king of Israel for seven days around 885 BCE, according to the Bible. A commander of chariots, he killed King Elah and his family at Tirzah, but the army proclaimed its general Omri king and besieged the city.

zeus-stratios.s: Zeus Stratios ('Zeus of the Army') was a god worshipped in Pontus and other parts of Anatolia, probably a Greek form of an Iranian sky god identified with Ahura Mazda. Appian describes Mithridates VI offering a great burnt sacrifice to him in the Persian manner, and a mountain…

zuiderzee-works.s: The Zuiderzee Works were a system of dams, dikes and land reclamation in the Netherlands, authorised in 1918 after a flood in 1916 and based on plans by the engineer Cornelis Lely. The Afsluitdijk, completed in 1932, turned the Zuiderzee into the freshwater IJsselmeer, and…

zama-regia.s: Zama Regia was an ancient town in north-western Tunisia, a royal residence of the Numidian kings, generally placed at the site of Jama near Siliana. It gave its name to the Battle of Zama of 202 BCE, fought somewhere in the region.

zhenbao-island.s: Zhenbao Island, known in Russian as Damansky Island, is a small island in the Ussuri River on the border between China and Russia. In March 1969 Chinese and Soviet troops fought deadly clashes there, the most serious episode of the Sino-Soviet border conflict, which brought…

zhou-enlai.s: Zhou Enlai was the first premier of the People's Republic of China, serving from 1949 until his death in 1976, and its foreign minister until 1958. A veteran of the Long March, he represented China at the Geneva Conference of 1954 and the Bandung Conference of 1955 and helped…

zia-ol-din-tabatabaee.s: Zia ol Din Tabatabaee was an Iranian journalist and politician who, with the Cossack officer Reza Khan, carried out the coup of 21 February 1921 that seized Tehran. He served as prime minister for about three months before Reza Khan forced him into exile.

zones-for-employment-and-economic-develo.n: Zones for Employment and Economic Development
zones-for-employment-and-economic-develo.s: Zones for Employment and Economic Development (ZEDEs) were semi-autonomous charter cities permitted under a Honduran law of 2013, with their own legal, tax and administrative systems run largely by private investors. The best known, Próspera on the island of Roatán, drew…

zondo-commission.s: The Zondo Commission, formally the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Allegations of State Capture, was a South African inquiry chaired by Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo from 2018 to 2022. It investigated how business associates of President Jacob Zuma, notably the Gupta…

zosimus.s: Zosimus was a Byzantine historian who wrote, around 500, a New History in Greek covering the Roman Empire from Augustus to the year 410. A pagan, he blamed Rome's decline on the abandonment of the traditional gods.

zidan-abu-maali.s: Zidan Abu Maali, known as Mulay Zidan, was a son of Ahmad al-Mansur and Saadi sultan of Morocco from 1603 to 1627. After his father's death he fought his brothers for the throne in a long civil war, eventually holding Marrakesh while rivals and religious leaders controlled…

zarinaea.s: Zarinaea is a legendary Saka queen known from the Persica of Ctesias, a Greek physician at the Persian court in the late fifth century BCE, and from later writers such as Diodorus. She is said to have fought the Medes, made peace with them and founded cities, and to have been…

zhang-yi.s: Zhang Yi was a political strategist of the Warring States period who served as chief minister of Qin. He promoted the 'horizontal alliance' (lianheng), persuading states to ally with Qin rather than unite against it.

zhanguo-ce.s: The Zhanguo ce, or Strategies of the Warring States, is a Chinese collection of speeches, anecdotes and diplomatic schemes from the fifth to the third century BCE, arranged by state. It was compiled by the Han scholar Liu Xiang in the first century BCE from earlier materials.

zou-yan.s: Zou Yan was a Chinese philosopher of the Warring States period associated with the Jixia Academy in Qi. He is regarded as the founder of the Yin-Yang school, combining the theory of yin and yang with the cycle of the Five Phases, which he used to explain the rise and fall of…

zhengguo-canal.s: The Zhengguo Canal was an irrigation canal in the State of Qin, begun in 246 BCE and named after its designer, Zheng Guo, an engineer from the State of Han. According to the Shiji, Han sent him to exhaust Qin's resources with a huge project, but the canal, linking the Jing and…

zanzibar-nationalist-party.s: The Zanzibar Nationalist Party was a political party founded in 1955 that campaigned for independence and drew much of its support from the Arab community and allied groups. In alliance with the Zanzibar and Pemba People's Party it formed the government when Zanzibar became…

zanzibar-revolution.s: The Zanzibar Revolution of 12 January 1964 overthrew the sultan and the government led by the Zanzibar Nationalist Party a month after independence. Insurgents led by John Okello and backed by Afro-Shirazi Party activists seized the islands; thousands of Arabs and South Asians…

zhao-rugu.s: Zhao Rugu was a member of the Song imperial clan who served as superintendent of maritime trade at Quanzhou in Fujian. About 1225 he wrote the Zhu Fan Zhi (Description of Foreign Peoples), which describes the countries, ports and products of maritime Asia and East Africa from…

zhol-pillar.s: The Zhol Pillar is a stone pillar inscribed in Old Tibetan that stands below the Potala Palace in Lhasa. Erected in the reign of Trisong Detsen, probably around 764, it records the services and rewards of the minister Takdra Lukhong, including his part in the Tibetan campaign…

zij-i-sultani.s: The Zij-i Sultani is the set of astronomical tables compiled at Ulugh Beg's observatory in Samarkand and completed around 1437. Written in Persian, it contains calendrical, trigonometric and planetary tables and a catalogue of about a thousand stars based on fresh…

zawar.s: Zawar is a mining area about 40 km south of Udaipur in Rajasthan and one of the oldest known centres of zinc production in the world. Mining there goes back more than two thousand years, and by the medieval period its smelters were distilling metallic zinc in clay retorts on a…

zaire.s: Zaire was the official name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997, adopted by Mobutu Sese Seko as part of his campaign of 'authenticity'. Under Mobutu's one-party rule the country, rich in copper, cobalt and diamonds, suffered from corruption and economic…

zadok.s: Zadok was a priest of King David and Solomon according to the Hebrew Bible. With the prophet Nathan he anointed Solomon king against the claims of Adonijah, whose supporter Abiathar was then banished, and he became the first high priest of the Temple in Jerusalem; his…

zumaque-i.s: Zumaque I was the oil well at Mene Grande, on the eastern side of Lake Maracaibo, that in 1914 became the first commercially productive well in Venezuela. Drilled by the Caribbean Petroleum Company, an affiliate of Royal Dutch Shell, it marked the start of large-scale oil…

zalesye.s: Zalesye ('the land beyond the woods') is the historical name of the north-eastern Rus' lands between the upper Volga and the Oka, centred on Rostov, Suzdal and Vladimir, which from the viewpoint of Kiev lay beyond the great forests. The region formed the core of…

zaki-khan-zand.s: Zaki Khan Zand was a half-brother of Karim Khan Zand, known for his cruelty. On Karim Khan's death in 1779 he seized power in Shiraz in the name of Karim Khan's young sons and had rivals killed, but his brutality turned his own troops against him, and he was murdered within…

zweibrucken.s: Zweibrücken is a town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, near the border with Saarland. It was the seat of the Counts of Zweibrücken and from 1453 of the Palatinate-Zweibrücken line of the Wittelsbachs, whose dukes later became kings of Sweden and of Bavaria.

zabdas.s: Zabdas was the leading general of Zenobia of Palmyra. In 270 he led the invasion of Roman Egypt, which brought the province into the Palmyrene Empire, and he helped extend Palmyrene control over Syria and Asia Minor.

zonians.s: Zonians were the American civilians who lived and worked in the Panama Canal Zone under United States administration from 1904 to 1979. Many were employees of the canal company and their families, living in subsidised company towns with their own schools, shops and police.

zenicetes.s: Zenicetes was a pirate chief who controlled Olympus, Phaselis and other places on the Lycian coast of southern Anatolia in the early 1st century BCE. When the Roman general Publius Servilius Vatia Isauricus captured his strongholds, around 77 BCE, Zenicetes set fire to his…

zela.s: Zela was an ancient city of Pontus in northern Anatolia, now Zile in Tokat Province, Turkey, built around a temple-state of the goddess Anaitis. Two battles were fought there: in 67 BCE Mithridates VI destroyed a Roman army under Triarius, and in 47 BCE Julius Caesar defeated…

zeno-of-laodicea.s: Zeno of Laodicea was a Greek orator of Laodicea on the Lycus in Asia Minor. In 40 BCE he persuaded his city to resist the Parthian invasion led by the Roman renegade Quintus Labienus.

ziesar.s: Ziesar is a small town in Brandenburg, Germany, west of Brandenburg an der Havel. From the 14th century it was the residence of the bishops of Brandenburg, whose castle with its Gothic chapel survives and houses a museum of the medieval diocese.

zenden.s: The Zenden (French dizains) were the self-governing communal districts of the Upper Valais, in present-day Switzerland. Seven of them, including Goms, Brig, Visp, Leuk and Sion, gradually took power from the prince-bishops of Sion in the 15th to 17th centuries and forced them…

zerbst.s: Zerbst is a town in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, north of the Elbe. From 1603 to 1793 it was the residence of the princes of Anhalt-Zerbst, who built a large baroque palace there.

zvenyhorod-lviv-oblast.s: Zvenyhorod is a village south-east of Lviv in western Ukraine, on the site of a medieval town that was the seat of a principality in the 11th and 12th centuries. Volodymyrko Volodarovych ruled from there before uniting Galicia, and the town was destroyed by the Mongols in 1241.

zhizdra-river.s: The Zhizdra is a river in Kaluga Oblast, Russia, a left tributary of the Oka about 220 km long. The medieval town of Kozelsk stands on it, famous for holding out against Batu Khan's Mongols for seven weeks in 1238, and the Optina Monastery lies on its bank.

zugdidi.s: Zugdidi is a city in western Georgia, the centre of Samegrelo, near the Enguri river and the boundary with Abkhazia. It was the main residence of the Dadiani princes of Mingrelia, whose palace complex is now a museum holding family treasures and relics of Napoleon acquired…

zungeru.s: Zungeru is a town in Niger State, central Nigeria. Frederick Lugard made it the capital of the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria in 1902, replacing Lokoja, and it remained the seat of government until the move to Kaduna in 1917.

zealots.s: The Zealots were a Jewish political and religious movement of the 1st century CE that sought to drive the Romans out of Judaea. During the First Jewish–Roman War a Zealot faction led by Eleazar ben Simon seized the Temple in 68, killed moderate leaders such as Ananus ben…

zabibe.s: Zabibe was a queen of the Arabs, probably of Qedar, in the 8th century BCE. She is named among the rulers who paid tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria in 738 BCE, alongside Rezin of Damascus, Hiram of Tyre and Menahem of Israel, and is the earliest of several Arab queens…

ziying.s: Ziying was the last ruler of the Qin dynasty. Placed on the throne in 207 BCE by the eunuch Zhao Gao after the Second Emperor's death, he had Zhao Gao killed and took the title King of Qin rather than emperor.

zugewandter-ort.s: A Zugewandter Ort (associated place) was a territory allied with the Old Swiss Confederacy without being a full member canton. Associates such as the Valais, the Three Leagues of the Grisons, the abbey and city of St.

zakopane.s: Zakopane is a town in southern Poland at the foot of the Tatra Mountains, in the Podhale region. It grew in the late 19th century into a mountain resort and an artistic centre, where Stanisław Witkiewicz developed the Zakopane style of architecture.

zamboanga-city.s: Zamboanga City is a port on the western tip of the Zamboanga Peninsula in Mindanao, in the southern Philippines. Spain built Fort Pilar there in 1635 as its main stronghold against the Moro sultanates of Mindanao and Sulu.

zimbabwe-african-national-union.s: The Zimbabwe African National Union (ZANU) was a nationalist movement formed in 1963 by a split from ZAPU, led from the mid-1970s by Robert Mugabe. Its armed wing, ZANLA, fought the Rhodesian government from bases in Mozambique.

zimbabwe-african-peoples-union.s: The Zimbabwe African People's Union (ZAPU) was a nationalist movement founded in 1961 under Joshua Nkomo to oppose white minority rule in Southern Rhodesia. Its armed wing, ZIPRA, fought the Rhodesian government from Zambia.

zafadola.s: Zafadola, as Christians called Ahmad Sayf al-Dawla, was the last prince of the Hudid dynasty of Zaragoza. Holding the castle of Rueda de Jalón, he became a vassal of Alfonso VII of Castile, exchanging Rueda for lands near Toledo, and tried to win power in al-Andalus as the…

zaranj.s: Zaranj is a city in south-western Afghanistan, capital of Nimruz province, on the border with Iran. As the chief town of Sistan in the early Islamic centuries, it was the base from which the Saffarid ruler Ya'qub ibn al-Layth rose to power in 861, and later the seat of the…

zusho-hiromichi.s: Zusho Hiromichi was a retainer of the Satsuma Domain who restored its ruined finances from the late 1820s. He forced the domain's creditors among the Osaka merchants to accept repayment of its huge debts over 250 years without interest, tightened the sugar monopoly in the…

zemun.s: Zemun is a district of Belgrade, Serbia, on the right bank of the Danube near its confluence with the Sava. Originally the Celtic stronghold of Taurunum, held by the Scordisci, it became a Roman fort and naval station on the Danube frontier.

zhang-zhizhong.s: Zhang Zhizhong was a Chinese Nationalist general who commanded in the battle of Shanghai in 1937 and later became a leading negotiator with the Communists. As head of the Nationalist administration in north-west China from 1946, he negotiated a coalition government for…

zoltan-tildy.s: Zoltán Tildy was a Hungarian Reformed pastor and leader of the Independent Smallholders' Party, which won the elections of November 1945. He became prime minister in 1945 and the first president of the Second Hungarian Republic in February 1946, but was forced to resign in…

zakare-mkhargrdzeli.s: Zakare Mkhargrdzeli was an Armenian-Georgian noble who served as commander-in-chief of the armies of Queen Tamar of Georgia. With his brother Ivane he won major victories against the Muslim powers and took Ani in 1199.

zhengzhou.s: Zhengzhou is the capital of Henan province in central China, a major railway hub near the Yellow River. Beneath the modern city lie the rammed-earth walls of an early Shang city of the Erligang period, about seven kilometres around, dating from about 1600 to 1400 BCE.

zhang-fei.s: Zhang Fei was a general of the late Han and Three Kingdoms period of China, a companion of Liu Bei from the start of his career together with Guan Yu. Famed for his courage and fierce temper, he held the bridge at Changban in 208 to cover Liu Bei's retreat.

ziusudra.s: Ziusudra is the hero of the Sumerian flood story, a king of Shuruppak warned by the god Enki to build a great boat and save life from the deluge. Afterwards the gods granted him eternal life and settled him in Dilmun, where the sun rises.

zariadres.s: Zariadres was a general of the Seleucid king Antiochus III, appointed governor of Sophene around 200 BCE while his colleague Artaxias received Greater Armenia. After Rome defeated Antiochus in 190–189 BCE, both governors declared themselves independent kings, and Zariadres…

zhaoqing.s: Zhaoqing is a city in western Guangdong, China, on the Xi River west of Guangzhou. In the 16th century it was the seat of the Ming viceroys of Guangdong and Guangxi, where the Jesuits Matteo Ricci and Michele Ruggieri set up their first mission in mainland China in 1583, and…

zhou-dynasty.s: The Zhou dynasty was the longest-ruling royal dynasty of China, which overthrew the Shang around 1046 BCE and nominally ruled until the State of Qin ended it in 256 BCE. Its kings granted lands to kinsmen and allies as hereditary states and justified their rule by the Mandate…

zuo-zhuan.s: The Zuo Zhuan is an ancient Chinese narrative history covering the period from 722 to 468 BCE, arranged as a commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals of the State of Lu. Traditionally attributed to Zuo Qiuming, it was probably compiled in the fourth century BCE.

zhengyang-county.s: Zhengyang County is a county in Zhumadian, in southern Henan province, China, near the Huai River. In antiquity it was the site of the State of Jiang, a small state of the Ying clan that allied with Qi and was destroyed by Chu in 623 BCE.

zhuangzi.s: Zhuangzi (Zhuang Zhou) was a Daoist philosopher of the 4th century BCE, a native of the State of Song. The book named after him, with the Laozi a founding text of Daoism, uses parable and paradox to question fixed values and celebrate spontaneity, as in his dream of being a…

zhaoge.s: Zhaoge was a city in northern Henan, near modern Qi County in Hebi, which served as a capital of the last Shang kings. After the Zhou conquest and the Rebellion of the Three Guards it became the capital of the State of Wey, granted to Kangshu Feng.

zhongyong-of-wu.s: Zhongyong was, in Chinese tradition, the second son of the Zhou chieftain Gugong Danfu and a brother of Taibo. With Taibo he gave up the succession and settled among the peoples of the lower Yangtze, where he succeeded his brother as ruler of Wu.

zhejiang.s: Zhejiang is a coastal province of eastern China, south of the Yangtze delta, with its capital at Hangzhou. It was the land of the ancient Yue peoples and the State of Yue, the kingdom of Wuyue in the 10th century and the heart of the Southern Song, whose capital was Hangzhou.

zichan.s: Zichan, personal name Gongsun Qiao, was chief minister of the State of Zheng from 543 BCE until his death in 522 BCE. He reorganised land and taxes, defended the small state between Jin and Chu by skilful diplomacy, and in 536 BCE had the penal laws cast on bronze vessels, the…
