zhuanxu.s: Zhuanxu is a legendary ruler of ancient China, counted among the Five Emperors and said to be a grandson of the Yellow Emperor. Several ruling houses of the Zhou period, including those of Chu, Qin and Zhu, claimed descent from him.

zoucheng.s: Zoucheng is a county-level city in south-western Shandong, just south of Qufu. It was the centre of the Zhou-period State of Zou and the birthplace of the philosopher Mencius, whose temple, family mansion and cemetery survive there.

zinder.s: Zinder is a city in south-central Niger and the country's second-largest. The capital of the Sultanate of Damagaram from the mid-18th century, it grew as a stop on the caravan route from Kano to Tripoli, and its old town and sultan's palace survive.

zainal-abidin-syah.s: Zainal Abidin Syah was sultan of Tidore in the Moluccas from 1947 until his death in 1967. After Indonesian independence he backed Indonesia's claim to Dutch-held West New Guinea, which Tidore had historically claimed as a dependency, and in 1956 he became the first governor…

zanabazar.s: Zanabazar was a Mongolian Buddhist leader and artist, the son of the Tüsheet Khan Gombodorj and the first Jebtsundamba Khutughtu, head of Buddhism in Khalkha. Trained in Tibet, he founded monasteries and in 1686 devised the Soyombo script.

zapotecs.s: The Zapotecs are an indigenous people of Oaxaca in southern Mexico. Their ancestors built Monte Albán, which from about 500 BCE to 800 CE was the capital of one of the first states of Mesoamerica, and later centres such as Mitla.

zamora.s: Zamora is a city on the Douro in Castile and León, Spain, capital of the province of Zamora. Fortified by the kings of Asturias in 893, it was a key stronghold on the Christian frontier along the Douro and was besieged repeatedly in the following centuries.

zhou-fohai.s: Zhou Fohai (1897–1948) was a Chinese politician who attended the founding congress of the Chinese Communist Party in 1921 before joining the Kuomintang. In 1940 he followed Wang Jingwei into the Japanese-backed Reorganised National Government at Nanjing, where he controlled…

zhu-lingshi.s: Zhu Lingshi was a general of the Eastern Jin dynasty in the service of Liu Yu, the future founder of the Liu Song dynasty. In 412 Liu Yu gave him command of an expedition against Qiao Zong's Western Shu in Sichuan.

zbruch-river.s: The Zbruch is a river in western Ukraine, a left tributary of the Dniester about 245 kilometres long, separating the historical regions of Galicia and Podolia. From 1772 to 1918 it formed part of the border between the Austrian and Russian empires, and between the world wars…

zhang-jianzhi.s: Zhang Jianzhi (625–706) was a Tang dynasty official who became chancellor under Wu Zetian in his old age. In 705 he led the coup that killed her favourites, the brothers Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong, and forced her to abdicate in favour of her son Zhongzong, restoring the…

zhou-dewei.s: Zhou Dewei (died 918) was a leading general of the Shatuo state of Jin in northern China during the transition from the Tang to the Five Dynasties. Sent by Li Cunxu against the Yan empire of Liu Shouguang in 911, he took Youzhou in 913 and then governed the region.

zerubbabel.s: Zerubbabel was a governor of the Persian province of Yehud and a descendant of the Judahite king Jehoiachin. According to the Hebrew Bible he led a group of exiles back from Babylon and, with the high priest Joshua, rebuilt the Temple in Jerusalem, completed around 516 BCE…

zangke-commandery.s: Zangke Commandery was an administrative region established by the Han dynasty in 111 BCE in the far south-west of China, mainly in modern Guizhou. It was created after the Han conquered Nanyue and the kingdom of Yelang submitted, and it extended Han rule over the south-western…

zuo-zongtang.s: Zuo Zongtang (1812–1885) was a Chinese statesman and general of the late Qing dynasty. He helped suppress the Taiping Rebellion, founded the Fuzhou Navy Yard and crushed the Dungan revolt in Shaanxi and Gansu.

zande-people.s: The Zande, or Azande, are a people of north-central Africa living in South Sudan, the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the south-east of the Central African Republic. From the 18th century the Avongara aristocracy built a series of conquest kingdoms among…

zanj.s: Zanj was the name that medieval Arabic and Persian writers gave to the Bantu-speaking peoples of the East African coast, which they called the land of the Zanj. Many Zanj were carried as slaves to Iraq, where those forced to clear the salt marshes near Basra rose in the Zanj…

zoque.s: The Zoque are an Indigenous people of western Chiapas and neighbouring parts of Oaxaca and Tabasco in Mexico, speaking a language of the Mixe-Zoque family, which many scholars link to the ancient Olmecs. In the late fifteenth century the Zapotecs took part of their lands on…

zabljak-crnojevica.s: Žabljak Crnojevića is a ruined fortified town on a rocky hill near the north-western shore of Lake Skadar in Montenegro. It was the seat of the Crnojević rulers of Zeta in the fifteenth century until Ivan Crnojević, under Ottoman pressure, moved to Cetinje in 1482.

zhou-wen.s: Zhou Wen was a general of Chen Sheng's Zhangchu during the Dazexiang uprising against the Qin dynasty. In 209 BCE he led a large rebel army through the Hangu Pass to within reach of the Qin capital Xianyang, but was driven back by the Qin general Zhang Han, who had armed…

zanu-pf.s: ZANU-PF, the Zimbabwe African National Union – Patriotic Front, is the ruling party of Zimbabwe. It grew out of ZANU, founded in 1963, which fought the guerrilla war against Rhodesia under Robert Mugabe, won the independence election of 1980 and absorbed Joshua Nkomo's ZAPU in…

ziri-ibn-manad.s: Ziri ibn Manad was a chief of the Sanhaja Berbers of the central Maghreb and a loyal ally of the Fatimid caliphs. He founded the fortress of Ashir around 936, helped the Fatimids against the Kharijite revolt of Abu Yazid in the 940s, and was killed in battle against the Zenata…

zabid.s: Zabid is a town in the Tihama coastal plain of western Yemen, founded around 820 by Muhammad ibn Ziyad as the capital of the Ziyadid dynasty. For centuries it was the main city of lowland Yemen and a leading centre of Sunni learning, with its Great Mosque and dozens of…

ziyad-ibn-abihi.s: Ziyad ibn Abihi, "Ziyad son of his father", was an Arab administrator of uncertain parentage who rose under the early caliphs. Having served Ali, he was won over by the Umayyad caliph Mu'awiya I, who acknowledged him as his half-brother and made him governor of Basra and then…

zabulistan.s: Zabulistan was a historical region of south-eastern Afghanistan around Ghazni and the upper valleys of the Helmand and Arghandab. From the late seventh century it was ruled by the Zunbil kings, who resisted the Arab conquest for nearly two centuries until the Saffarid Ya'qub…

zamindawar.s: Zamindawar is a historical region in the upper Helmand valley of southern Afghanistan, now part of Helmand province. In the early Islamic period it held a famous shrine of the god Zun, linked to the Zunbil kings, and Arab armies struggled for two centuries to control it.

zun.s: Zun was a god worshipped in southern Afghanistan before and during the early Islamic period, at a famous shrine at Zamindawar in the upper Helmand valley. Arab writers describe a golden idol with ruby eyes; the cult may have links to sun worship or to Hindu deities.
